Both religions became popular as they opposed the varna and jati systems of the Hindu religion.

correctItems.text: The Mauryan pillars are rock- cut pillars thus displaying the carver's skills, whereas the Achamenian pillars are constructed in pieces by a mason.
Stone pillars were erected by Ashoka, which have been found in the north Indian part of the Mauryan Empire with inscriptions engraved on them.
The Mauryan pillar capital found at Sarnath popularly known as the Lion Capital is the finest example of Mauryan sculptural tradition.
This pillar capital symbolising Dhammachakrapravartana (the first sermon by the Buddha) has become a standard symbol of this great historical event in the life of the Buddha.
